pairs.evidence: src/features/agents/sub_executions/libs/useBulkRerun.ts:165 The bulk-rerun cohort (original run vs re-run, both able to fail) averages cost and duration deltas over every pair that has both figures, whatever its outcome, and shows no both-succeeded view and no subset count, so a re-run that is cheaper only because it failed early reads as a saving.

techniques.evidence: src/features/agents/sub_executions/libs/useBulkRerun.ts:165 Delta is taken over all priced pairs regardless of success or failure. There is no conditioned (both-succeeded) figure beside it, and costDeltaN is never shown. Also, the success rate's denominator counts timed_out rows, which hit the view's own 15-minute wait budget (a harness-owned stop), as non-success.

src/features/agents/sub_executions/libs/useBulkRerun.ts:177 A single re-sample that disagrees with the original is labelled a 'regression' (or 'recovery'). The technique calls an n=1 re-run a second sample, not a correction.

src/features/agents/sub_executions/components/list/BulkRerunReport.tsx:113 The report lists losing rows (regressions) in their own section beside the headline success rate, so the headline does not hide them.
